bib.title: RAFT: Adapting Language Model to Domain Specific RAG

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "RAFT: Adapting Language Model to Domain Specific RAG", Tianjun Zhang, Shishir G. Patil, Naman Jain, Sheng Shen, Matei Zaharia, Ion Stoica, Joseph E. Gonzalez (UC Berkeley). arXiv 2403.10131v2, 5 Jun 2024. Header reads "Preprint, Under Review" (no venue in the PDF). Code: github.com/ShishirPatil/gorilla.

COVERAGE: all 41,482 chars read (every page, references included). No appendices. Extraction is clean. Figure 5 and 6 plots have no numeric data in the text (axes only).

CLAIMS
1. RAFT (LLaMA2-7B) beats the baselines on 4 of 5 datasets and ties on a fifth.
 number: Table 1 below
 setup: LLaMA2-7B-chat base; RAFT trained on 1 golden doc + 4 distractors; GPT-3.5 + RAG for reference. The metric is not named in the text; the paper only says "accuracy" in the figure axes.
 quote: "RAFT (LLaMA2-7B) 73.30 35.28 74.00 84.95 86.86"
 where: p.5, Table 1
 Table 1 (PubMed / HotPot / HuggingFace / Torch Hub / TensorFlow):
 - GPT-3.5 + RAG: 71.60 / 41.5 / 29.08 / 60.21 / 65.59
 - LLaMA2-7B: 56.5 / 0.54 / 0.22 / 0 / 0
 - LLaMA2-7B + RAG: 58.8 / 0.03 / 26.43 / 08.60 / 43.06
 - DSF: 59.7 / 6.38 / 61.06 / 84.94 / 86.56
 - DSF + RAG: 71.6 / 4.41 / 42.59 / 82.80 / 60.29
 - RAFT: 73.30 / 35.28 / 74.00 / 84.95 / 86.86
 Caveats from the table: GPT-3.5 + RAG scores higher on HotPot (41.5 vs 35.28). RAFT's margins over DSF on Torch Hub and TensorFlow are 0.01 and 0.30 points. On PubMed, RAFT beats DSF + RAG by 1.7 points.

2. Adding RAG to a domain-finetuned model does not reliably help. The authors suggest the model was never trained to process context.
 number: DSF vs DSF + RAG: HotPot 6.38 to 4.41; HuggingFace 61.06 to 42.59; Torch Hub 84.94 to 82.80; TensorFlow 86.56 to 60.29; PubMed 59.7 to 71.6 (the only gain)
 quote: "introducing RAG to a domain-specifically fine-tuned (DSF) model doesn't invariably lead to better outcomes. This might indicate that the model lacks training in context processing and extracting useful information from it."
 where: p.6, Sec 4.1

3. Stated gains. Over base Llama-2: "The gain can be as big as 35.25% on Hotpot QA and 76.35% on Torch Hub evaluation." Over DSF: "30.87% on Hotpot and 31.41% on HuggingFace".
 setup: the base is probably LLaMA2-7B + RAG. Check against Table 1: 35.28 - 0.03 = 35.25, and 84.95 - 8.60 = 76.35. These are absolute points, though the text writes "%". For the DSF comparison, 35.28 - 4.41 = 30.87 (HotPot) and 74.00 - 42.59 = 31.41 (HuggingFace), so those are against DSF + RAG, not plain DSF.
 quote: "RAFT does much better on the tasks like Hotpot and HuggingFace datasets (30.87% on Hotpot and 31.41% on HuggingFace)."
 where: p.6, Sec 4.1

4. Chain-of-thought answers with verbatim quotes help (ablation).
 number: Table 2 (PubMed / HotpotQA / HuggingFace / Torch Hub / TensorFlow). RAFT w/o CoT: 68.30 / 25.62 / 59.07 / 86.56 / 83.21. RAFT: 73.30 / 35.28 / 74.00 / 84.95 / 86.86. Torch Hub is worse with CoT (84.95 vs 86.56).
 quote: "With a gains of 9.66% and 14.93% in the Hotpot QA and HuggingFace datasets respectively."
 setup: CoT answers generated with GPT-4-1106; the answer cites the source passage between ##begin_quote## and ##end_quote##. Gorilla APIBench answers already include reasoning.
 where: p.7, Table 2; p.6, Sec 4.2

5. Train with some examples where the golden document is absent (fraction P kept with the golden doc). The paper reports P = 80% as helpful, but its optimum varies by dataset.
 number: "P% ranging from 40%, 60%, and 100%" across NQ, TQA, HotpotQA (the text does not map each value to a dataset). Fig. 5 shows no numeric data in the text.
 setup: 1 golden + 4 distractors at train and test.
 quote: "incorporating a portion of the training data without the golden document in the context (P = 80%) appears to enhance the model's performance on RAG tasks."
 where: p.7-8, Sec 4.4, Fig. 5
 Note: the P = 80% in the text and the 40/60/100% optima do not agree. This is an inconsistency inside the paper.

6. Training with distractors makes the model robust to a varying number of test-time docs. Training on the golden doc alone does worse.
 number: optimal training setup differs by dataset: NQ D*+3D (text) vs "4 documents" (Fig. 6 caption); Trivia QA 3 docs; HotPot QA D*+1D (text) vs "2" (caption). The authors still use 1 golden + 4 distractors throughout. Fig. 6 plots only NQ and HotPot (the caption mentions three domains).
 quote: "finetuning with only the golden document frequently results in inferior performance compared to configurations that include a greater number of distractor documents."
 setup: trained with varying distractors; evaluated with top-3 retrieved docs, and with top-k from 2 to 10 for Fig. 6.
 where: p.8-9, Sec 5.1, Fig. 6

7. Method: for a fraction P of questions the training example is Q + D* + distractors; for the remaining 1-P it is Q + distractors only. Both are labelled with a CoT answer A*. This is supervised fine-tuning, and RAFT is independent of the retriever.
 quote: "P % of data: Q + D∗ + D1 + D2 + . . . + Dk → A∗ (1 − P) % of data: Q + D1 + D2 + . . . + Dk → A∗"
 where: p.4, Sec 3

8. The authors' stated reason for the no-golden-doc fraction is memorization, and the motivation for distractors is distraction in top-k.
 quote: "By removing the golden documents in some instances, we are compelling the model to memorize answers instead of deriving them from the context."
 where: p.4, Sec 3. Citing Shi et al. 2023a (irrelevant context distraction): "top-k RAG is frequently employed at test time to ensure high recall" (p.8).

9. Qualitative HotPot example: DSF answers "The Family Man" (a film) where the question asks for a screenwriter; RAFT answers "David Weissman".
 where: p.7, Fig. 4

LIMITS
- Scope is in-domain only: the test uses the same document set as training. The authors contrast this with other work: "our paper studies a slightly opposite scenario where we only care about testing the LLM on the same set of documents." Out-of-domain transfer is not shown.
- Only LLaMA2-7B was finetuned; no other model sizes or families.
- Metrics are not defined in the text. No variance, seeds or confidence intervals. The NQ and TQA numbers appear only in plots.
- Table 1 omits NQ and TQA, though the datasets section lists them.
- PubMed gains are small; the authors attribute this to yes/no questions.
- Baselines: DSF and RAG numbers are likely tied to a particular prompt style. The authors say Llama-7B "performs poorly due to its answering style not aligning with the ground truth", so a share of the gain is style alignment, not reading ability.
- The text-versus-caption inconsistencies in claims 5 and 6 are unresolved.
- Dated: 2024, LLaMA-2 era. The authors do not test long-context models.

BUILDS ON: Lewis et al. 2020 (RAG); Wei et al. 2022 (chain of thought); Patil et al. 2023 (Gorilla, APIBench); Shi et al. 2023a (LLMs easily distracted by irrelevant context); Liu et al. 2023 (Lost in the middle); Weston and Sukhbaatar 2023 (System 2 Attention); related fine-tuning-for-RAG work: RA-DIT (Lin et al. 2023), InstructRetro (Wang et al. 2023), Xu et al. 2023 (Retrieval meets long context), ChatQA (Liu et al. 2024); Atlas (Izacard et al. 2023), RETRO (Borgeaud et al. 2022), kNN-LM, REPLUG, Self-RAG (Asai et al. 2023). Datasets: HotpotQA (Yang et al. 2018), PubMedQA (Jin et al. 2019), NQ (Kwiatkowski et al. 2019), TriviaQA (Joshi et al. 2017). Self-Instruct (Wang et al. 2022) is cited for "practice QA"; LIMA (Zhou et al. 2023) for SFT alignment.

CODE: none in the paper. Prompt in Fig. 3 (p.5), verbatim: "Instruction: Given the question, context and answer above, provide a logical reasoning for that answer. Please use the format of: ##Reason: {reason} ##Answer: {answer}." The answer format is "##Reason: ... ##begin_quote## ... ##end_quote## ... ##Answer: Delhi".

FIGURES
- Fig. 1 (p.2): closed-book vs open-book vs RAFT, the exam analogy. Fastest way to explain the motivation.
- Fig. 2 (p.3): RAFT overview, golden plus distractor docs in training, standard top-k at test.
- Fig. 3 (p.5): CoT generation prompt and example with quote markers.
- Fig. 4 (p.7): RAFT vs DSF qualitative example.
- Fig. 5 (p.8): accuracy vs P% golden for NQ, TQA, HoPo.
- Fig. 6 (p.9): accuracy vs top-k test docs for each number of training distractors.
I did not run the figure-caption script; these are taken from the extracted text.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. The Fig. 3 caption does not match its content: it describes a self-critique prompt, but the figure shows a CoT generation prompt. A stray "[0/1879]" appears in the HotPot question text. The plot values in Fig. 5 and 6 could not be extracted. The paper's text and captions conflict on the best number of training distractors (claim 6) and on the best P (claim 5).
